title: Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2608.19689v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based social simulation is a promising complement to traditional methods such as surveys and behavioral experiments. A core question is how to evaluate the fidelity of LLM-simulated human behavior and optimize LLMs toward it. Prevailing practice evaluates by accuracy, checking whether the model selects the single response observed from a human, and trains the LLM to reproduce this hard label. However, human behavior is inherently subjective: the same person in the same situation may reasonably act differently, so an observed response is only one draw from an underlying response distribution, rendering accuracy-based evaluation unreliable and hard-label training misleading. translated_title: 重新思考基于大语言模型的社会模拟的评估与优化
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型的社会模拟是对传统方法（如调查和行为实验）的一种有前景的补充。核心问题在于如何评估大语言模型模拟人类行为的保真度，并据此优化大语言模型。当前的主流实践通过准确性进行评估，检查模型是否选择了从人类观察到的单一响应，并训练大语言模型以复现这种硬标签。然而，人类行为本质上是主观的：同一个人在相同情境下可能合理地做出不同行为，因此观察到的响应只是潜在响应分布中的一次抽样，这使得基于准确性的评估不可靠，硬标签训练也具有误导性。为解决这些问题，我们首先引入了主观性系数，这是一种基于熵的量，用于区分客观任务（如编码）和主观任务（如社会模拟），并利用它系统性地分析了基于准确性的评估如何受到影响。
tldr: 本文提出主观性系数来识别主观任务，并指出基于准确性的评估和硬标签训练在社会模拟中不可靠，为改进评估与优化方法奠定基础。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a subjectivity coefficient to distinguish subjective tasks and shows that accuracy-based evaluation and hard-label training are unreliable for social simulation, laying groundwork for improved evaluation and optimization methods.
